accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA A-level Chemistry 3.3.5 Alcohols (classification, oxidation by acidified potassium dichromate(VI), distillation for aldehydes, reflux for acids, [O] equations), OCR A 4.2.1 and Edexcel Topic 6. Boiling points used: ethanal 20 °C, propanal 48 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C, propanoic acid 141 °C. Tertiary alcohols resist because the carbinol carbon has no H; Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange, +6) is reduced to Cr³⁺ (green, +3).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets classifying by total carbons or by branching (first prediction, 2-methylpropan-1-ol as primary in m3 and the challenge, tag size), expecting all alcohols to oxidise (tube prediction, tag tert), expecting a secondary alcohol to reach an acid (product rows, tag ketone), mixing up distillation and reflux (kit prediction, tag reflux) and saying the dichromate is oxidised (m5, tag colour).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagalcox moves an –OH bead round a branched 2-methylbutane skeleton, warms three alcohols in tubes, strips H atoms from a displayed C–OH centre to build C=O, switches between distillation and reflux apparatus and predicts four products. flagalc (the earlier Alcohols lesson) covers different ground, and the 6-token shingle gate passed at under 30 percent.

lab_teaches.evidence: The evidence appears before the rule: the same five carbons give 1°, 2° and 3° as the –OH moves, two tubes go green while the tertiary stays orange, the tertiary centre refuses to form C=O because there is no C–H to remove, and the receiving flask collects propanal while reflux leaves propanoic acid in the flask.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with plausible distractors: total carbons or branching as the basis of classification, all three tubes turning green, and propanal as the reflux product. A.reveal shows the learner's guess next to the observed result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating exam-style questions tagged size, tert, reflux, ketone and colour; why() gives the chemical reason, for example reflux sends the aldehyde back into the oxidant so it goes on to the acid. Product rows explain each wrong choice, such as making butanone would need a C–C bond to break.

readability.evidence: Learner audience for ages 16–18: kid text scores 5.7 and adult text 8.7 on the FK check, inside the limits, with exact specification terms: primary, secondary, tertiary, carbinol carbon, acidified potassium dichromate(VI), aldehyde, ketone, carboxylic acid, reflux, distillation and [O].

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with the existing Alcohols and Oxidation and reduction lessons is under 12 percent. Each paragraph adds one idea: classification, the colour test, products by class, then apparatus; the adult text adds equations, boiling-point reasoning, Tollens' and Fehling's tests and named mistakes.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 light and Android 360 px light and dark screenshots after every Show me. The –OH on C2 was moved below the chain after it overlapped the branch carbon, long tube names wrap onto two lines, and the classification label was shortened to fit 360 px. Every action has a button twin.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs and axe checks run in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with all five Show me tasks completing. Tube results are given in words (green, stays orange) as well as colour, and the canvas aria-label speaks each classification and observation.
